In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

HIV-1 evolution in the proviral compartment is not always associated with systemic viremia and that the proviral diversity is a complex trait that depends on the host immune response, the level of systemic viremia, and other factors.
HIV controllers represent a heterogeneous group, with different patterns of intra-host HIV- 1 evolution and viral suppression.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the HIV-1 reservoir in HIV-1 controllers can be heterogeneous, with some subjects displaying highly divergent proviral populations with low diversity and others displaying highly homogeneous populations with high intra-host diversity.
there is a considerable variation in intra-host proviral evolution and diversity among elite controllers.

the intra-host evolution of HIV-1 is a dynamic process that can be affected by several factors including viral suppression level, viral load set-point, immune control and host genetic factors, among other factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV controllers are not a homogeneous group of subjects and that a detailed analysis of their intra-host HIV- 1 evolution may reveal different mechanisms that underlie the control of HIV replication.

the intra-host HIV diversity and rate of evolution in elite and viremic controllers are not necessarily correlated with the systemic viral suppression and that ongoing evolution of the HIV- 1 reservoir in PBMC is possible even in individuals with persistent undetectability.

the intra-host evolution of HIV-1 in the proviral compartment is highly heterogeneous even in the same group of HIV controllers, which may reflect different mechanisms of HIV-1 suppression in the host and/or distinct patterns of proviral evolution in the PBMC compartment.
